title: Feeding and Nutrition Management
description: Standard operating procedure for proper feed storage, handling, and administration in aquaculture operations. Covers species-specific feeding schedules, feed quantity calculations, feeding observation protocols, and nutritional management for optimal organism growth and health. Applicable to all cultured organism types.

steps.title: Feed Quality and Safety
steps.description: Only use feed that meets quality standards. Never use moldy, rancid, or expired feed as it can cause disease, mortality, and contaminate systems. Compromised feed is a biosecurity risk and economic loss.
checklistItems: Check feed expiration date before use
Inspect feed for mold, discoloration, or off-odors
Verify feed storage conditions were maintained
Confirm feed type matches species requirements

steps.title: Feed Storage Requirements
steps.description: Proper feed storage is critical for maintaining nutritional value and preventing contamination. Store dry feeds in cool, dry conditions below 25C (77F) with humidity under 70%. Frozen feeds must remain at -20C or below. Refrigerated feeds at 2-4C. Use FIFO (First In, First Out) inventory management.

steps.title: Daily Feed Storage Inspection
steps.description: Perform daily inspection of feed storage areas to ensure proper conditions and inventory levels.
checklistItems: Storage area temperature within acceptable range
Humidity levels acceptable for dry feed storage
Freezer temperatures verified for frozen feeds
No signs of pest activity (rodents, insects)
Inventory levels adequate for upcoming needs

steps.title: Feed Handling Hygiene
steps.description: Maintain strict hygiene when handling feed to prevent cross-contamination. Wash hands before handling feed. Use clean, dry scoops and containers. Never return uneaten feed to storage containers. Clean up spills immediately.

steps.title: Species-Specific Feed Types
steps.description: Different organisms require different feed types. Finfish: Pelleted feeds sized to mouth gape. Coral: Microalgae, rotifers, copepods, and coral-specific feeds. Oysters/Bivalves: Live microalgae or algae paste. Kelp/Seagrass: Nutrient supplementation via water. Always confirm appropriate feed type for your species and life stage.

steps.title: Calculate Daily Feed Ration
steps.description: Calculate the appropriate daily feed ration based on organism biomass, species, life stage, water temperature, and growth targets. General formula: Daily ration = (Total biomass kg) x (% body weight feed rate). Feed rates typically range from 1-10% body weight depending on species and temperature. Document calculations.

steps.title: Pre-Feeding System Check
steps.description: Before feeding, verify system conditions are appropriate. Feeding during stress or poor water quality wastes feed and can exacerbate problems.
checklistItems: Water quality parameters within acceptable range

steps.title: Do Not Feed If
steps.description: Withhold feeding if organisms show signs of stress, disease, or if water quality is compromised. Feeding stressed animals wastes feed and can accelerate health decline. Common signs to watch for: lethargy, loss of color, rapid respiration, surface gasping, or abnormal behavior.
checklistItems: DO NOT feed if DO is below 4 mg/L
DO NOT feed during disease treatment unless directed
DO NOT feed if ammonia exceeds 0.5 mg/L
DO NOT feed if organisms show disease symptoms
DO NOT feed during extreme temperature events

steps.title: Prepare Feed
steps.description: Weigh out the calculated feed ration using calibrated scales. For frozen feeds, thaw in clean, refrigerated conditions before use. For live feeds, culture and harvest according to separate protocols. Never over-prepare feed as quality degrades quickly once opened or thawed.

steps.title: Feeding Technique - Broadcast Feeding
steps.description: For broadcast feeding (common with finfish and coral): Distribute feed evenly across the water surface or growing area. Feed slowly in small amounts, allowing organisms to consume before adding more. Total feeding time should be 5-15 minutes depending on species. Avoid dumping large amounts at once.

steps.title: Feeding Technique - Automated Systems
steps.description: For automated feeding systems: Verify hopper is loaded correctly. Check feed size matches dispenser settings. Confirm timer settings are correct. Observe at least one automated feeding cycle daily to verify proper operation. Clean feeders weekly or as needed.

steps.title: Feeding Technique - Filter Feeders
steps.description: For filter-feeding organisms (oysters, mussels, coral): Introduce microalgae or particulate feeds into the water column. Maintain appropriate flow rates to suspend feed particles. Monitor water clarity to gauge feeding response. Too much feed causes water quality degradation.

steps.title: Feeding Observation
steps.description: Observe organisms during and immediately after feeding. Feeding behavior is an important indicator of health and appropriate ration size.
checklistItems: All areas of tank/system receiving feed
Feed being consumed within appropriate time

steps.title: Adjust Feed Ration Based on Observations
steps.description: Adjust feeding amounts based on observations. If feed is consumed rapidly with organisms still actively searching, consider slight increase. If significant feed remains after 15-20 minutes, reduce ration. Document adjustments and rationale.

steps.title: Remove Uneaten Feed
steps.description: Remove uneaten feed from systems to prevent water quality degradation. Use nets, siphons, or mechanical removal as appropriate. Excessive uneaten feed indicates overfeeding or health/appetite issues requiring investigation.

steps.title: Feeding Schedule Guidelines
steps.description: Feeding frequency varies by organism and life stage. Larvae: 4-6 times daily. Juveniles: 2-4 times daily. Adults: 1-2 times daily. Coral: 2-3 times weekly to daily depending on species. Cold water species: Reduce frequency at lower temperatures. Maintain consistent feeding times when possible.

steps.title: Post-Feeding Documentation
steps.description: Document all feeding activities for tracking, analysis, and regulatory compliance.
checklistItems: Date and time of feeding recorded
Feed type and lot number logged

steps.title: Clean Feeding Equipment
steps.description: Clean all feeding equipment after use. Rinse scoops, buckets, and feeders with freshwater. Allow to dry completely before storage. Regular cleaning prevents biofilm buildup and cross-contamination between systems.

steps.title: Feed Contamination Response
steps.description: If feed contamination is suspected or confirmed, immediately remove all affected feed from use. Quarantine and inspect remaining inventory from the same lot. Notify supervisor and document incident. Monitor organisms for adverse effects for 48-72 hours.
checklistItems: Remove contaminated feed from all systems
Contact supplier if product defect suspected
